The question's premise does not match the document: NFA-F did not show the best capacity retention. The paper names NFA-A as the most retentive variant, at ≈80%[1] capacity retention after 100[2] cycles, compared with ≈68%[3] for the NCA cathode.

In the capacity-retention figure, the NFA-F curve is the lowest of the curves after the cycling test, below the other NFA variants and the NCA curve. Fig. 8[4]

The text gives ≈70%[5] as the retention value for the other cobalt-free variant named there, and no retention value for NFA-F is stated in the text.

The paper does not explain why NFA-F retained less capacity; it gives no mechanism specific to that composition. Its only general remark on fade is that structural transitions can cause capacity fade[6]. NFA-F is LiNi0.8Fe0.15Al0.05O2[7] with 5% Al[8], the lowest aluminum content of the variants.
